title: Installing a Below-Grade Toilet with a Macerator Pump (This Old House)
summary: This Old House demonstrates installing a toilet below grade using a macerator unit behind the toilet. The video contrasts a standard siphon-jet toilet with a P-trap style discharge fed by a macerator, explains how waste is pumped through a small-diameter line to tie into the house drain, covers venting to the vent stack, and shows the practical steps of rough-in, priming and cementing PVC joints, securing the fixture to the subfloor with brass lag screws, connecting the toilet to the macerator with a rubber gasket and clamps, and finally restoring the water supply to test the tank fill.
topics: lavatory drain connection to macerator reservoir
toilet mounting without a closet flange

sections.description: The presenters compare a standard siphon-jet toilet with a P-trap style unit that discharges toward the back, emphasize the macerator behind the toilet, and explain that waste is pumped through a small-diameter line up the wall toward the house drainage system.

The vent is described as tying into the vent stack, and a lavatory drain is connected to the macerator reservoir.

sections.description: The toilet is positioned and anchored using brass lag screws into the subfloor, a rubber accordion gasket and hose clamps create the seal between the toilet outlet and the macerator, and the water supply is restored to verify the tank fills correctly.
